description: Add an opt-in blocking pull-request publication mode for task worktrees: when enabled by policy, publication pushes the task branch to origin, opens a GitHub PR against main via gh CLI, records PR metadata in the task run dir, and defers main advancement and worktree cleanup until the human-merged PR makes the task commit an ancestor of canonical HEAD; the existing fast-forward flow remains the default when the flag is off, and the finish gate requirement (commit integrated into canonical branch) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: With the policy flag off, task publication behaves exactly as today (fast-forward integration + finish gate unchanged): regression test proves identical behavior on a fixture task.

With the policy flag on, publication pushes the task branch to origin, creates a PR against main using gh CLI with a rendered title/body carrying task provenance, records PR URL/number/branch in the task run dir, and does NOT fast-forward main, NOT remove the worktree and NOT release the writer lock at that point.

After the PR is merged and canonical HEAD advances (fetch/pull), an explicit finalize step completes cleanup (worktree removal + lock release) and publish_status then reports published=true for the integrated commit; the finish gate passes unchanged.
Behavioral tests cover the three states (pre-merge, merged-withOUT finalize, merged-with finalize) via fixture fakes for git/gh invocations, without network access.

origin.decision: Repository owner selected, in orchestrator session chat, the blocking-PR publication mode (PR blocks task closure; human performs the merge) for future tasks, answering the orchestrator's flow-design question
origin.source_task_context: POKER-HAND-EVAL-001 closure discussion (canonical flow integrates directly to main; owner requested PR-based delivery 'lo del PR que es lo mejor')

planning.title: Opt-in blocking PR publication mode for task worktrees
planning.notes: Additive design required: do not modify scripts/worktree.py core publish semantics in this task; reuse its typed primitives by import and implement the PR flow as a new module plus a new policy file with the flag defaulting to off. gh CLI availability is an external runtime contract; tests must fake the gh invocation.
